adds.rationale: Tanker rates have been surging on Iran-Israel war-premium and sanctions-driven rerouting of Russian/Venezuelan crude, and Frontline's Q2 2025 print (profit beat, forward VLCC charters, fleet renewal) turns the profile's named-but-uncovered tactical tanker/freight exposure into a concrete, liquid holding.

news_evidence.summary: Frontline reported Q2 2025 results: $80.4M adjusted profit on higher TCE rates, no major debt maturities until 2030, plus new one-year time charter-out agreements on seven VLCCs and a fleet renewal initiative.

The Iran-Israel 12-Day War (June 2025) pushed Strait of Hormuz war-risk insurance and charter rates up sharply, and U.S. sanctions on Russian and Venezuelan oil pushed tonne-miles and floating storage higher, keeping tanker markets tight through Q3 2025.

adds.rationale: Firefly Aerospace's Nasdaq debut adds a second pure-play launch/lander name alongside RKLB and ASTS, giving earlier-stage exposure to the commercial Moon/launch buildup the profile flags as the top-priority next wave.

news_evidence.summary: Firefly Aerospace completed its Nasdaq IPO on August 7, 2025, raising approximately $868 million, and began trading under ticker FLY.
Firefly's Blue Ghost Mission 1 achieved the first fully successful commercial soft Moon landing, the commercial heritage underpinning the IPO thesis.

rationale_overall: Net effect: two adds bring the watchlist to the 24-ticker cap by filling a genuine gap (zero tanker/commodity exposure despite the profile explicitly watching energy/commodity cycles, with a live Q3 catalyst in Hormuz war-premium plus Russia/Venezuela sanctions rerouting) and by deepening the rockets & spacecraft leg with a second pure-play IPO (FLY) alongside RKLB/ASTS. No removes: nuclear (SMR/OKLO/CCJ/BWXT, reinforced by the Sept 2 2025 TVA-ENTRA1 6GW SMR deal), quantum (IONQ/RGTI/QBTS, each with fresh contract wins), defense (ITA/LMT/GD/AVAV, with AVAV's record Q1 FY26 print offsetting LMT's July 22 program-charge guidance cut, a legacy-program execution issue rather than a rearmament-thesis breach), robotics (SYM/ROK, both with in-window momentum) and demographics (ISRG) all still show intact buildup theses. Considered but skipped: KOID (humanoid-robotics ETF, launched June 2025) — too new by Sept 30 to confirm it clears the liquidity floor; left for a future rebalance.
